column1: # Red-case fixture for the PR-title ticket-ID rule (KB-116, KB-121).
#   expect = pass | fail   -- whether the rule ACCEPTS this PR
#   body   = the PR description body, or "-" for none (null).
#            Use \n for a newline. The body is what carries the escape hatch.
#   title  = the FULL PR title, prefix included.
# Two things changed in KB-121 and both matter when adding rows:
#   1. Rows are now full titles, not bare subjects. The pattern is anchored at
#      the end of the title, so it never needed the `type(scope):` prefix
#      stripped -- which is why the rule could stop being a `subjectPattern`
#      on the semantic-pull-request action and move into code we can test.
#   2. The body column exists at all. Before KB-121 the escape hatch lived in
#      a GitHub expression no test could reach, so the table proved only half
#      the rule. These rows are the other half, end to end.
# CONTRIBUTING.md "Enforcement Mechanisms" requires a demonstrated red case,
# re-proven after every edit. This table is that proof, and CI runs it on every
# PR -- so the mechanism re-demonstrates it can still reject bad input rather
# than having been seen working once at introduction.
# Add a row whenever the rule changes. A row marked fail that starts passing is
# the regression this file exists to catch.
# --- the bug this fixture was created for: digit-bearing team keys (KB-116) ---
# --- team keys without digits must keep working ---
# --- wrong brackets: the mistake authors actually make ---

column1: # --- the hatch must not fire on near-misses ---
# The marker must OWN ITS LINE. The GitHub expression this replaced used
# contains(), which matched anywhere -- so a PR that merely DISCUSSED the hatch
# was exempted by it. Observed live: PR #85, which introduced the rule module,
# was itself waved through on its first CI run because its body explains what
# [noticket] does. Its title carried a valid [KB-121] that was never checked.
